UI thread stuck in Activity.performStop -> WindowManagerGlobal.setStoppedState
(Handler.runWithScissors), waiting for the game thread, which sits in

background so the game thread can drain its Looper.

TOTK: opt-in TOTK_SYNC_LAG lets the game's per-frame GPU wait lag one submission

The game's main thread (observed_main) waits every frame on the fence of the
submission it has just made, so its CPU frame never overlaps the GPU frame
(~7 ms blocked per frame in a heavy world scene on an M4 MacBook Air).
TOTK_SYNC_LAG=1 (runtime: "flag sync_lag 0|1", off by default) makes such a
wait settle for the previous submission. With the translation thread the
newest submission must still be translated before the wait returns, so the
game never rewrites command memory that is still being read.

Random numbers from a Random you can seed, fork and pass around

Random is a seeded generator with the helpers as methods. `random` is the
game's own (also `game.random`), which the free functions draw from, and it's
always seeded: `new Game({ seed })`, or one it picks and the template logs,
with ?seed= to play a run again. `fork(name)` replaces reseedIfSeeded and
makeRandom with sequences worked out from the seed and a name, and
`cosmeticRandom` keeps looks and sound (the engine's sound code) from
changing a seeded run. rRound now rounds to the nearer integer more often;
it did the opposite.

Keep NPCs from stepping away when the player bumps into them

The game's bump reaction moves NPCs 75-128 units away from a player who
walks into them, so in VR they back off from reaching hands. Set the bump
move distances to fBumpMoveDistance (default 0) at start.

loop later ended with an IOException, Studio stopped receiving game events
until it was restarted: the dead loop also stayed in `listener`, so TryStart
reported success without listening.

TryStart every tick while the pipe is not listening. The pipe name is a
constructor parameter so the test can use its own pipe. Removes unused Start().

keeps it in XInput. `play start --mode` changes the pad to the input mode
of the profile, and `play stop` changes it back.

and `play stop` changes it last, after the RAM state is back: the save
then writes the state from before the game

the page and ask whether it changed, an unchanged page answers 304 with no
body, and a new game version is still picked up on the next visit.

feat: [HIMMEL-3054] burstpin.sh shortens DXVK's launch compile burst

Even with warm NVIDIA and DXVK caches, every launch spends minutes with
DXVK's pipeline-library workers pegging the CPUs the game is pinned to.
burstpin.sh wraps the launch command and lets the background workers
(dxvk-shader-n/-l) of the new game process use 90 % of all CPUs at nice
10; with dxvk.numCompilerThreads = 40 the Overwatch burst on a 7950X3D
drops from ~230 s to ~115 s. README explains the burst, the measurements
and which CPUs it helps (dual-CCD X3D with the game pinned: most).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Place actors by the save as it loads, not by the old game

Loading kept the old game's whereabouts until the next refresh (up to 20 s):
actors the old game had touched spawned where it had them, untouched ones by
its clock's schedules, GetCurrentPackage answered its packages, and the
refresh then followed door changes against its packages, which could relock
or unlock home doors and drop saved home warnings. Snapshot::apply now
rebuilds the table from the save before its cells load, keeping the package
caches, and takes the packages found as the ones home doors last followed.

therefore written as 0, and overlapping geometry in that range was

fix: don't time out the LAN manifest fetch while the host hashes

The host's /manifest handler blake3-hashes the whole game folder on
first request. That takes about 1 s/GB on an SSD and much longer on a
hard drive, so the fixed 300 s total timeout failed installs of large
games with "operation timed out".

Drop the total timeout on that request. The shared client now has a
10 s connect timeout and TCP keepalive so an unreachable or vanished
peer still errors, and the existing cancel poll lets the user abort.

* Lazy copy-on-write buffer[T] on dotnet and the JVM (D226, #8389)

A managed buffer is a handle over its storage: a copy marks the storage
shared in O(1) and the first write after it makes the storage private.
Also: record .copy copies a buffer field, array-of-buffer copies no longer
emit an unresolvable JVM intrinsic, and native evaluates a buffer write's
index and value before making the buffer unique.

Keep the MSVC vtable layout of the data stores outside of MSVC

The engine calls the data stores through the vtable of its own MSVC build. A
virtual destructor is one slot there (scalar deleting destructor) but two with
GCC/MinGW, which moved every function after it by one: the engine called read()
and ended up in write(), which aborts. Custom maps that load game assets
through the asset database crashed the game.

Outside of MSVC the destructor is replaced by a function in the same slot.

Sounds are mono 16-bit samples at MIXER_RATE in one mixer, whether decoded
from a WAV file (any SDL-readable format is converted) or generated by the
game and copied in with set_sound. Music is a callback the game provides,
with a gain and its own switch; sound effects have their own switch and a

Keep enemies, pickups, bullets, effects and particles in engine pools

Every collection of things that come and go is now an engine object_pool
instead of a fixed array with an alive flag: the pool is the single record of
what is alive, the game walks it with pool_next_active, and objects are
released by pointer. The world is built with world_new, restarted in place
with world_restart and released with world_free, so it owns its pools.

Tests and golden snapshots are unchanged.

Keep jinput from probing the input devices, whose stale close(0) aborted the game

On a machine that cannot open /dev/input, jinput's native nClose runs on a device that never opened and closes descriptor 0. The first close frees stdin, the next descriptor any thread opens is then 0, and the second close removes it under that thread. The file watcher's directory stream was the victim, and Rust's closedir panics on the resulting EBADF, which aborts the game (#562). Sound: the mixer and the game's thread no longer wait on each other

The mixer holds its lock a voice at a time, not for a whole chunk's mix:
when the game's thread wants the lock (mixer_lock_wanted, which every
taking of the lock but the mixer's own says) the mixer lets it in between
voices. The game's thread no longer waits for the lock to tell streams
their finished packets: a trylock, and a stream whose lock is held is told
the next frame. And 256 frames are mixed at a time rather than 1024, so a
sound started or stopped waits out at most 5 ms of mixing; at 1024 each
such call was up to 2.

Infra: run the API Lambda at 1024 MB (0.58 vCPU, up from 0.29) (#479)

Lambda CPU scales with memory. At 512 MB a request's own CPU work — zod, JSON,
the game-code sandbox start, cold init — was the floor under every score post
and games-list read: prod p50 for the dry-run preview was 318 ms around 45 ms
of actual work. 1024 MB is ~0.58 vCPU; billing is per GB-second, so a request
that finishes in proportionally less time costs about the same.
